title: File system - Do not crash when a volume cannot be mounted
intro: A volume that failed while mounting could return with its journal or root still live, and the next use crashed. Those objects are now released on the journal, block allocator, and root-node failure paths. Proof: haiku-pi star row 50, commit 9799738757.

title: Kernel - Read a large fragmented file without crashing
intro: Finishing one piece of a split read used to call back into the same completion path and overflow the stack on a large fragmented file. The completion now loops, and a nested finish is remembered until the loop can take it.

title: Runtime loader - Load a per-thread value from a library
intro: A startup library built for initial-exec thread-local storage did not load on x8664, because those relocations were rejected. Storing the symbol value plus the addend would not land on the variable.

title: File system - Delete a folder while the disk is being synced
intro: Deleting a folder while the disk was being synced could leave a vnode reference behind, because the finished-I/O hook used the shell path in the kernel. The kernel path now drops the vnode through the VFS. The shell path is unchanged.

title: USB storage - Unplug a disk without stalling its transfer
intro: Unplugging a USB disk during a transfer could wait on the device lock while the transfer still held it. A transfer that finds the device already gone finishes at once, and the schedulers are deleted before that lock is taken for the last time.

title: Kernel - Stop a profiler timer when the program stops
intro: A profiler timer could keep firing after the program had stopped. The timer is cancelled when the thread exits, replaced, or is no longer the installed one, and a thread with a profiler timer is marked unscheduled when it switches out.

title: Kernel - Keep a shared file shared after its protection changes
intro: Changing the protection of a shared file mapping inserted a private copy, so the mapping stopped sharing and a later fork no longer saw the same pages. A file cache is no longer copied for that reason. The existing shared-area flag is left as it is.

title: Kernel - Save the last changed pages before power is lost
intro: The page writer used to go back to waiting when its timer ran out, so the last modified pages were left unwritten until a sync. A timeout now falls through and those pages are written. The under-quota wait stays.

title: GPU M5 - Every program gets its own protected GPU memory
intro: When gfx9vmidperfile is on, each open render node builds its own page table and takes a VMID from 2-15. VMID 1 stays the shared table. The setting stays off, so a normal boot still submits every job on VMID 1.

title: Tools - Refuse a stick image that cannot boot
intro: The M5 stick did not boot: it was written from the raw VM image (@r5-raw), which starts with a BFS boot sector and has no partition table. The 5625U boots by EFI and needs the anyboot image (@r5-anyboot), like stick 29.

title: Tools - One script to write a USB stick
intro: Writing a test stick took long every time: Cursor tried PowerShell first, which never worked, and then wrote a new Python script (write26.py, write27.py, write29.py) in the ignored generated/ folder, so the next stick started from nothing again.

title: System - Keep thread-local data when a library is unloaded
intro: A new thread-local vector no longer starts at generation 0. Unloading a library with thread-local storage then does not zero the blocks that thread just created. The file is Haiku's elftls.cpp (copyright 2014 Paweł Dziepak, MIT).

title: GPU - Do not load firmware on an unknown graphics chip
intro: An unknown PCI id no longer loads Green Sardine firmware. r5gfx9fwstemfor() follows the four ids already in the radeonhd device table. 1636 and 164c stay renoir. 15e7 (Barcelo) and 1638 (Cezanne) stay greensardine. Any other id returns NULL.

title: Kernel - End a program instead of letting it crash in an endless loop
intro: row 22. haiku-pi commit 6e517bb52c (kernel: a fault whose signal is blocked or ignored ends the team). This branch also contains ★ row 20, haiku-pi commit 6f810ed2d7.

title: Kernel - Fix a crash while a program is being closed
intro: row 43. haiku-pi commit e09cfa1d9e (kernel/thread: keep an exited thread's stack while its team goes down). A signal that ends a team is handled by one thread, which exits at once.

title: Kernel - Fix a kernel crash when memory can only be partly locked
intro: row 20. haiku-pi commit 6f810ed2d7 (kernel/vm: lockmemoryetc(): unwire what was wired when a page fails). lockmemoryetc() left a wired range at its full size when a later page could not be wired. The revert looked for the shorter size and panicked.

title: VirtualBox - Switch the audio driver so the VM shuts down cleanly
intro: The R5 VM hung in about half of the power-offs. In the VirtualBox logs, R5 always reached S5 (ACPI power down), and then VirtualBox did not finish turning off its devices (no PDMR3PowerOff line, the state stays POWERINGOFF, and the VM ends up aborted).

title: Audio - Safer and more accurate USB audio and MIDI
intro: Points A1–A7 and M1 of the usbaudio and usbmidi review. Kernel safety (A1–A3). The mix, buffer and description ioctls no longer size stack arrays or an alloca from the caller's counts, and they check user pointers.

title: MIDI 2.0 - Fix translations, device names and the parser
intro: The MIDI 2.0 spray calls, the MIDI 1.0 translation, and the parsers that lived in the public headers. SprayNoteOn(0, 60, 100) is a MIDI 1.0 note again. The 16-bit and 32-bit calls are SprayNoteOn2 and SprayControlChange2.

title: Boot - New icons on the boot screen
intro: The boot loader reads kSplashIcons24BitCompressedImage from images-sans-tm.h. That header is checked in, and jam does not rebuild it, so copying splashicons.png into data/artwork never reached the screen.

title: Desktop - New disk icon and a wider About window
intro: The system disk and VBox Share use the silver drive. The boot disk still carries the R5 mark where the ladybug sat. Other disks, including VBox Share, use the same drive without the ladybug.

title: Docs - Guide to the Appearance Kit classes
intro: New docs/APPEARANCE-KIT.md: what the Appearance Kit is (BeOS-style classes in BAppearanceKit, one header per class, MIT, in libr5ui.so), a table of the classes with when to use them and when not, and what a new class needs in the same change.

title: Developers - MIT license for the interface libraries, and the new BCard
intro: libr5ui and libr5icons are MIT, so an application can link them. BAppearanceKit::BCard is a rounded group in libr5ui. About R5 is the first caller: a document card for the heading and a panel card with the system information in a 2×2 grid.

title: Boot - White boot screen and the finished logo
intro: The boot splash is white, the boot volume uses the ordinary hard disk, About splits the version from the build, and About's icon is the Wave Pebble. The splash is 372 by 96 on white, with the dark wordmark and no border. A 24-bit boot screen clears to white.

title: Design - Brand guide for the R5 look
intro: The Wave Pebble SVG is the only drawing of the mark. scripts/generate-r5-artwork.py writes the pictures from it, and --check compares the product files. apply-overlay.sh runs that check. The boot splash and its BGR are pure black (#000000).

title: Docs - README update for M4 and MIDI 2.0
intro: Build 10048. Vulkan through RADV on AMD Renoir is an experimental opt-in; the desktop is still drawn by the CPU. MIDI 2.0 support. Merge after the MIDI boot of #4110.

title: System - Bring in the latest Haiku changes
intro: The Haiku tree is a subtree merge of upstream/master (4aae8640c9). Nothing in that merge was reverted. archtimer.cpp in the Haiku tree is the upstream file. The image builds the distro/ copy.

title: GPU M4 - Fix the second Vulkan program drawing the wrong picture
intro: On the Ryzen 5 5625U, with the radeonhd settings on: vulkaninfo names the GPU as AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV RENOIR), next to llvmpipe. VulkanTeapot draws the teapot through RADV, offscreen, copies the picture into a bitmap, and shows the device name.

title: M4 - R5 GPU interface and RADV on the Radeon (Renoir), experimental and off by default
intro: The first GPU path of R5 Operating System. It is experimental and off by default. Nothing changes for a user unless the radeonhd driver settings switch it on. The software path stays installed and stays the default: appserver Painter, llvmpipe and Lavapipe.

title: Roadmap - Bring in the haiku-pi bug fixes now
intro: One line in docs/ROADMAP.md, under "x86-64 fixes from haiku-pi": the timing changes from "after M5" to "now". The fixes go on their own branch from main, in small PRs per group, and do not wait for the GPU PRs (#4108, #4111).

title: Design - Add the reference picture for the R5 window look
intro: Two new files, no code: docs/design/sign-in-reference.jpg: the user's reference for how an R5 window should eventually look, shared on 7 Nov 2026; docs/design/README.md: what to take from it, and how R5 gets there.

title: GPU - Plan a driver kit that makes adding a GPU easy
intro: Documentation only: docs/GPU-ARCHITECTURE.md (a new section "GPU Driver Kit", and one open decision) and one bullet in docs/ROADMAP.md. Decided on 7 Nov 2026: anyone who knows a chip should be able to add it to R5 quickly. A driver author: 1.

title: Roadmap - Take work from other Haiku forks: haiku-pi, air/OS and RenkuOS
intro: docs/ROADMAP.md only. No code. Decided on 7 Nov 2026: R5 takes what already works in other Haiku forks, and builds itself only where R5 is deliberately different. That covers the GPU interface, multi-user, the Settings window and the BeOS-style kits.

title: Tracker - Open folders in the same window, with the navigator
intro: In R5, Tracker now opens a double-clicked folder in the same window and shows the navigator (Back, Forward, Up, and the location bar). Haiku's default opens a new window for each folder.

title: Roadmap - Graphics Kit after M7
intro: Documentation only: a Graphics Kit section in docs/ROADMAP.md (Graphics and media). Nothing is built. Names, BeOS style. The Graphics Kit, named after the domain like the Interface Kit and the Media Kit.

title: M5 plan - One GPU address space per program
intro: Documentation only: the M5 decisions in docs/GPU-ARCHITECTURE.md. One GPU address space per open render node; every context in that file shares it. VMIDs 1–15 are assigned per submission (as Linux amdgpuvmidgrab), with a TLB flush when a VMID is reused.

title: M4 - VulkanTeapot uses the freeglut teapot geometry
intro: VulkanTeapot builds the Newell teapot the way freeglut 3.4 fghTeaset does: convert each control point to GL (x, z - 1.575, -y) times one half, turn patches 0–5 around that Y axis, and mirror patches 6–9 on GL Z with the row order reversed.

title: M4 - VulkanTeapot keeps drawing after the window opens
intro: A double-click of VulkanTeapot opened an empty window. The bitmap was drawn once, immediately after Show(), and the first update cleared it. The program also rendered only one frame, and the title repeated the device name.

title: Roadmap - Platform section (CPU, power, firmware)
intro: Adds "Platform (CPU, power and firmware)" to docs/ROADMAP.md. Each item has where R5 stands, what it takes, and the hardware needed to test it: P-states.

title: M4 - Vulkan path: RADV with a GPU, Lavapipe without
intro: The render node speaks the R5 GPU interface. libdrm translates the ioctl set RADV uses, and the image ships Mesa with RADV next to Lavapipe. VulkanTeapot draws one offscreen frame and prints the device.

title: M4 plan - Vendor-neutral GPU interface, VMID 1, Intel track
intro: Updates the GPU plan for M4 and the Intel work, and brings in the render-node and Zink decisions that #4097 missed. docs/GPU-ARCHITECTURE.md Licence correction (decision 4). Most Linux amdgpu files carry an MIT-style notice, and most of i915 is MIT.

title: M3 - Kernel driver owns the GPU: interrupts and GART
intro: The kernel driver starts the fixed GFX9 sequences when gfx9ring and gfx9kernel are set. The accelerant then logs GFX9 owned by the kernel and does not start the command processor again. gfx9irq and gfx9gart stay separate opt-in keys.

title: GPU plan - Licence, Mesa recipe and VulkanTeapot decisions
intro: Records five decisions the owner made on 5 Nov 2026, in docs/GPU-ARCHITECTURE.md and the GPU section of AGENTS.md: 1. The R5 GPU interface header and the R5 DRM library are MIT. This is a deliberate exception to the GPL-3.0 default.

title: Docs - Roadmap, AGENTS review and the R5 name
intro: Four documentation commits: 1. AGENTS.md review (faf257cafe). This was already pushed to #4093, but #4093 was merged before it arrived. Prose says R5. About shows Version YYYY.N-dev Build N.

title: Docs - AGENTS.md up to date, and the M2 compute rule
M2 - GFX9 compute dispatch after the fence
intro: Milestone M2 for R5. After the GFX9 fence has landed, and only when the radeonhd settings say gfx9compute true, the command processor runs four compute dispatches. The shader source is gfx9compute.s, assembled with LLVM 18.1.8.

title: GPU plan - Architecture, and the R5 name rule
intro: Adds docs/GPU-ARCHITECTURE.md, the plan for 2D and 3D rendering on the GPU in R5 Operating System (R5), and records the product name. Decisions in the document: Haiku applications keep their APIs and the libbe ABI. The GPU is an extra backend behind them.

title: M1 - GFX9 IB and DMA fill after the fence
intro: After the GFX9 fence has landed, an opt-in workload asks the GPU to write memory. The first check is an indirect buffer: WRITEDATA of 0xDEADBEEF, then RELEASEMEM.

title: Docs - README for readers
intro: The old README mixed feature notes, build steps and policy in long paragraphs, and it was out of date. It named build 10038, said haiku/ is not in this repository, and missed the sound and graphics work.

title: M0 - GFX9 ring and fence: load Renoir firmware through the PSP
intro: The radeonhd table follows the Linux v6.12 device list. New DCE families and the catch-all row stay off. The visible VRAM pool is the PCI framebuffer window with the firmware picture reserved. The doorbell BAR is mapped. PSP v12 loads the GC 9.3 firmware.

title: Tree - Copy the remaining Haiku sources into the R5 tree
intro: distro/rest now holds the Haiku sources that the apply scripts still rewrote in place: the network stack and net server, package volume, input, DriveSetup, accounts and the locked preferences, LaunchDaemon, Installer, the boot prompt, About, Deskbar…

title: Tree - Copy kernel and desktop Haiku sources into the R5 tree
intro: Interface, Tracker, Deskbar, locale, the control look, and the related preference and appserver files now live in distro/desktop. archtimer.cpp and archcpu.cpp live in distro/kernel.

title: Hardware - Skip DCN encoder DPMS and ship family 19h microcode
intro: Barcelo (1002:15e7) stays claimed. On Raven and later, radeonhd returns before encoder DPMS and before the unfinished R600 command-ring reset. CONFIGMEMSIZE of 0xffffffff is logged as unused; the PCI aperture stays the upper bound.

title: Hardware - Keep the Barcelo desktop on the firmware scanout
intro: The 17:38 Europe/Amsterdam stick booted on the Ryzen 5 5625U and reached the desktop. radeonhd claimed 1002:15e7 (Barcelo, revision c2) and mapped the bootloader framebuffer at 1920x1080, pitch 7680, physical 0xfce0000000. eDP attached from the boot EDID.

title: Tools - Read BeFS from Windows and prepare the next 5625U boot
intro: A read-only BeFS reader for Windows lives in this tree, because there is no separate toolchain repository. py -3 tools/r5-befs/r5befs.py lists a directory and exports a file from a raw image, an anyboot MBR, or a physical drive with an offset.

title: Apps - Record the WebPositive jam in the changelog
intro: The address-bar fix compiled, and that jam result did not land in the changelog with the code. jam -q WebPositive for AMD64 finished at 12:51 Europe/Amsterdam on 3 Nov 2026 with exit 0. A background tab was not opened.

title: Apps - Keep the WebPositive address bar when a background tab starts loading
intro: Middle-clicking a link opens a tab without selecting it. LoadNegotiating still wrote that URL into the address bar, and a later update put the current page back (Haiku #20319, GitHub #3953). The bar looked as if the open page was being replaced.

title: Apps - Bound the TextSearch grep scanset to the file-name array
intro: Grepper stored a grep line in a buffer twice as long as fileName, then parsed the name with %[^n:]. A long line, or the remainder of a line that fgets had split, wrote past fileName and TextSearch crashed (Haiku #14485, GitHub #1785).

title: Apps - Report the Terminal wheel when mouse tracking is on
intro: On the alternate screen, Terminal turned the mouse wheel into arrow or page keys. A full-screen program that had enabled mouse reporting then received keys instead of a scroll (Haiku #20409, GitHub #4014).

title: Mail - Stop the POP3 flush when the server has closed
intro: POP3Protocol::SendCommand drained leftover bytes before each command. A closed socket stays readable, and Read returns 0, so the loop printed Had to flush 0 bytes and never returned. That is the maildaemon core spin in Haiku #14441 (GitHub #1771).

title: Mail - Parse mail dates that use the obsolete UT zone
intro: ParseDateWithTimeZone() left a trailing UT for parsedate(). That function accepts GMT and UTC and rejects UT, so the date failed and the mail's When time became the moment it was fetched (Haiku #20440, GitHub #4031).

title: Network - Keep an HTTP timeout that is set before the socket exists
intro: BNetworkRequest::SetTimeout() wrote the timeout only when a socket was already open. BHttpRequest creates that socket later, inside MakeRequest(), so a timeout set before the request starts was lost (Haiku #20436, GitHub #4028).

title: Audio - Keep the mixer alive when no sound device is connected
intro: A late-buffer notice and the buffer-group request both followed fCore->Output() without a check. With no sound device that pointer is empty, and mediaaddonserver crashes (Haiku #20425, GitHub #4023). Both calls return when the output is missing.

title: Audio - Record the USB audio guest test and close the host tickets
intro: The VirtualBox guest from the 11:42 Europe/Amsterdam image was reported good at 11:49 the same morning. PR #4072 is merged (5440628b7e). Haiku #19472, #18842, #18994, #20149, and #20323 are marked fixed. The note records that report.

title: Audio - Name HDMI outputs and add a headphone surround mix
intro: An HDMI pin with no device type was shown as HDMI  (Haiku #20171). The output is named HDMI. Analog converters keep their format. An HDMI converter is added only when it supports that format, and DigEn enables it.

title: Audio - Keep USB audio from double-locking EHCI and halting xHCI
intro: USB audio on EHCI took the isochronous lock in the finish thread and again when the callback queued the next packet. That is the double-lock KDL (Haiku #19472, GitHub #3554).

title: Audio - Add USB Audio Class 2.0 and a channel layout setting
intro: USB audio accepted only class 1.0 and skipped any alternate with more than two channels. A class 2.0 device was not recognised. usbaudio now accepts a class 2.0 control header (0x0200).

title: MIDI 2.0 - Record the guest midi2test run
intro: The VirtualBox guest from the 10:53 Europe/Amsterdam image ran midi2test and printed all checks passed (reported at 10:55). That includes per-note controllers, profiles, endpoint and function-block discovery, the USB descriptor helpers, and the earlier MIDI…

title: MIDI 2.0 - Add per-note controllers, profiles, and discovery
intro: Per-note controllers are one type 0x4 UMP. Apps send them with SprayUMP. NoteOn and ControlChange are not called for that packet. MIDI-CI Profiles (inquiry, set on/off, enabled/disabled reports, profile specific data) use the existing System Exclusive path.

title: MIDI 2.0 - Add MIDI-CI Property Exchange to libmidi2
intro: An application could send notes and SysEx, and could not ask a device for DeviceInfo or subscribe to a resource. Property Exchange is MIDI-CI System Exclusive in libmidi2. Requests, replies, and subscriptions share a request id.

title: MIDI 2.0 - Receive full MIDI 2.0 values and reassemble SysEx7
intro: Incoming UMP was reduced to 7-bit MIDI 1.0 before an application could read it, and usbmidi returned BUNSUPPORTED for SysEx on a version 2.0 endpoint. Data still receives the Universal MIDI Packet.

title: Audio - Save the latency choice for the signed-in account
intro: Pull request #4064 merged before the permission fix. Media still could not create hda.settings, because config/settings/kernel/drivers stays root until r5-desktop gives it to the signed-in account.

title: Audio - Latency, media fixes, and basic MIDI 2.0
intro: Media preferences can ask for a shorter HD Audio or USB audio buffer. The choice is written to the driver settings, and a failed save shows the path. Build 10043 still reported Permission denied. The image ships config/settings/kernel/drivers as root.

title: Audio - Resample the mixer with cubic Hermite
intro: High quality in the mixer follows the curve of four neighbouring samples instead of a straight line between two. The same-rate path is still a copy. Drop/repeat samples is unchanged. A 48 kHz MP3 into the 48 kHz mixer crashed in AudioMixer control.

title: Fix audio hot-plug, packed 24-bit, and mixer latency
intro: Stability fixes in the media stack, then a smaller mixer latency path. The copied Haiku files keep their MIT headers and live in distro/media/. scripts/apply-media.py copies them into the Haiku tree.

title: Rebuild Fonts and Look and Feel from the Appearance preference
intro: Fonts and Look and Feel are separate Personalization pages again, rebuilt from the old Appearance preference views. The broken Settings Appearance module is gone. The separate Appearance program stays installed.

title: Add the Appearance page and the desktop picture
intro: Appearance is a page in Settings, with Fonts, Colors, Look and feel, and Antialiasing. A change is applied at once. The separate Appearance program stays installed. The tab body fills the area under the tabs. Workspace columns and rows stay one line.

title: Freeze the Settings list order and five descriptions
intro: The Settings list order and five descriptions stay as they are until the user explicitly asks to change them. Another Settings task does not include reordering the list or rewriting those lines. Information stays first under System.

title: Put Information first and shorten five Settings lines
intro: Information is the first page under System. Every other page, in every category, is alphabetical by name. The cards on a category page use that same order.

title: Add a locked Display page and bold Settings box titles
intro: Settings has a Display page under System. It is locked until an administrator opens the lock. Resolution, colors, and refresh wait for Apply, then ask to keep the picture. After 12 seconds the previous picture returns.

title: Open Settings narrower so Defaults stays on screen
intro: Settings opens at 1030 by 610. The list and Search are 200 wide. A home card is at least 280. The shortest size is 910 by 560. Build 10035. What's new says Settings opens a little narrower.

title: Add the Settings lock and Virtual memory
intro: Settings has a lock between Home and Revert. r5buttonsetlock() in libr5icons.so draws Haiku's ActionLogin when it is open and ActionLogout when it is closed. A page that requires an administrator stays gray, and nothing is written, until that lock is open.

title: Add Notifications to Settings
intro: Settings has a Notifications page under System. A change is written immediately to the notification server's settings file. Where a message appears is a screen picture: the four corners, or against the Deskbar. The default place is the lower right.

title: Add Desktop and Deskbar to Settings
intro: Settings has a Desktop and Deskbar page under Personalization. Save messages the running Deskbar. The separate Deskbar preferences program stays installed. A later commit removes Save. A change is applied immediately.

title: Ship Settings icons and the libr5icons shared library
intro: Settings page icons and home cards get the Haiku preferences wrench. About R5 does not. Back and Home are icon buttons, the same height as Revert and Save, in that order. Those two icons do not get the wrench.

title: Finish Settings: Wallpaper, Information, and a fixed frame
intro: The earlier Settings pull request merged before these follow-ups. Wallpaper menus no longer overlap, and choosing Image after Workspace no longer locks the window. The window opens shorter.

title: Add a Settings window with category cards
intro: Settings is one preference window: a sidebar, search, and a single content area. Home and each category use the same cards, with the existing preference icon on the left. A category page does not repeat its summary under the title.

title: Software Vulkan: vulkaninfo names llvmpipe, session owns the shader cache
intro: Software Vulkan on the CPU is the next Mesa step. vulkaninfo 1.4.367 is packed as vulkantools, Lavapipe’s ICD manifest is under add-ons/vulkan/icd.d (where the Haiku loader searches), and the image pin installs that package.

title: Follow the formatting country on the Deskbar clock
intro: Dutch (Netherlands) and the 24-hour choice now update the Deskbar clock without waiting for a saved settings file. Moving Nederlands above English reloads the catalogs, so Trash can become Prullenbak.

title: Read AMD P-states and Intel HWP without writing them
intro: The kernel now prints a read-only CPU snapshot and publishes the same text at /dev/misc/r5pstate. No MSR is written. On AMD and Hygon it reads the hardware P-state table when that CPUID bit is set, and the CPPC registers when that bit is set.

title: Ship build 10023 control fixes
intro: A program filling a text box no longer sends the modification message. Typing still does (#11735). A second click on the same slider value still sends the message (#13680). Scrollbar arrows stay off when the whole range is already visible (#6873).

title: Record eight closed Haiku issues
intro: The GitHub mirror now marks eight Haiku tickets closed. Each issue has a comment that quotes the status note. Issue #96 is not one of them. #290 Haiku 4154, #637 Haiku 7644, #1001 Haiku 9974 #1415 Haiku 12859, #1874 Haiku 14900, #2581 Haiku 16968 #2022 Haiku…

title: Translate well-known folders and keep icon names full
intro: Well-known folders (system, home, apps, preferences, develop, config) use their catalog name when the folder has no SYS:NAME attribute (#15527). Other folders are unchanged, so #10200 stays open.

title: Drop the leaf menu scroll arrows in build 10022
intro: The leaf menu no longer shows an up arrow and a down arrow when the items fit on the screen. The 4px placement margin is still used when a menu would hang off the edge, and scrolling still turns on when the menu is actually taller than the screen.

title: Mirror Haiku tickets and ship build 10021
intro: Every open Haiku Trac ticket is mirrored to GitHub (scripts/sync-github-issues.py, tracker/github.tsv). An issue already marked fixed on main is closed with a comment that quotes the status note. A closed issue stays closed when Trac still lists the ticket.

title: Fix thirty Tracker and Deskbar bugs and the Desktop share overlap
intro: ﻿Tracker and Deskbar in build 10019 keep a long name inside the copy window, and that window grows with the font. The finish time no longer shows a date in 1901. Escape clears a selection. Opening the parent folder keeps that folder selected.

title: Close the other Deskbar menu bar before opening one
intro: No upstream commit names #20099. The leaf menu and the running-apps list are two BMenuBars in one window. Each one replaced the window menu semaphore and left the other menu tracking.

title: Keep box and separator labels inside the view at large font sizes
intro: No upstream commit names #11625, #18518, or #18813. scripts/apply-ui-bugs.py: sizes a BBox label to the full line, including leading, and draws the baseline on the ascent so the top of the glyphs stays inside the view (#11625, #18518) uses that same line…

title: Use control colors for flat buttons, scrollbar arrows, and plain text
intro: Haiku's June 2025 control-color rework is already in this tree. upstream/master (fetched 1 Nov 2026) has no newer commit for these tickets. Gerrit 11871 for #20372 was abandoned, so styled text runs stay as they are.

title: Compile OpenGL against Mesa 25 and keep the GPU plan
intro: The Mesa 25 image on main still compiled OpenGL apps against the Mesa 22 devel package and swapped packages after jam. These commits pin libglvnd and Mesa 25.3.6 before jam, copy What's new into About, and leave Mesa 22 out of the solver.

intro: The daily image no longer keeps Mesa 22. Jam still compiles OpenGL apps against the Mesa 22 devel package. After the image is written, scripts/install-mesa-packages.sh removes mesa-22.0.5-3, mesadevel-22.0.5-3, and mesaswpipe-22.0.5-3, and adds: libglvnd…

intro: The Licenses tab now uses the same green headings as What's new. A line that is only a web address is a link. Under that summary, the tab lists the same components Credits already lists, including libprint, with the same license-file and site links.

title: Add an About Licenses tab
intro: About gains a Licenses tab next to Credits and What's new. The VirtualBox GPL paragraph is no longer in the Credits introduction. Credits still names people and projects, with a short VirtualBox line.

intro: R5OS-owned files now carry SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 R5OS Contributors and SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later. Haiku copies under distro/ keep their original copyright and license. The AirPlay RAOP server stays MIT because it follows Shairport.

intro: Sign-in starts the VirtualBox guest tools only when /dev/misc/vboxguest exists. The desktop follows the window, and each host share is mounted on the Desktop as VBox Share. The image is 2048 MB (build 10015).

title: Ship VirtualBox guest additions on the daily image
intro: The daily image now installs the VirtualBox 7.2.22 Haiku guest additions, together with the GNU GPL version 3 text and the matching source. Build 10014. What's new and About both say this build includes GPL version 3 code.

title: Record throwaway VirtualBox display and resize results

intro: The second boot no longer sticks on the rocket. The registrar reads /etc/passwd itself instead of calling getpwnam() while it is still starting. Sign in does not list the system account root.

title: Record the multi-license policy and point the README at it
intro: R5OS is not an MIT-only tree. This records the policy that was only in local notes, and points the README at it. docs/LICENSING.md is the policy. New files that R5OS owns default to GPL-3.0-or-later when R5OS can license the whole file.

title: Stop the boot loader waiting forever for a missing CPU
intro: A cold VirtualBox start with two CPUs often never left the boot splash: no icon lit, and the machine could sit that way for hours. Serial stopped at the boot loader line kernel entry at ….

title: Cover the signed-in session with a lock screen
intro: Deskbar → Lock screen covers the current session. Tracker and Deskbar stay running. Login does not call StartSession and does not clear the session file. Unlock checks the password of the person in the session file.

title: Lock printers, repositories, and swap on the machine
intro: Printers, Repositories, and VirtualMemory use the same bottom-right lock as Network. Printer queues live under /boot/system/settings/printers for every account.

title: Show each person their own account card
intro: Users & Accounts is a card: picture, name, username, email, and Change password. A standard account sees only that card and can edit it while the machine lock is on. An administrator, or Unlock, also sees the people list and Add / Disable / Delete.

title: Show Log out with the account name and reach Sign in after Restart
intro: After the first Sign in, uid 0 is locked root with home /boot/system. Autologin still starts that uid-0 session so Login stays uid 0. /boot/system is packagefs, so Restart and a cold boot stayed on the splash instead of Sign in.

title: Lock machine preferences for a standard account
intro: Network, Screen, Time, and Users & Accounts stay in Preferences for everyone. Nothing is hidden by role. An administrator changes them immediately. A standard account sees the same window with a lock at the bottom right.

title: Give every account the yellow leaf-menu folders
intro: Sign in already starts the desktop as the chosen account. Folder icons still did not match. nicky saw the old yellow folders in the leaf menu.

title: Sign in starts the desktop as that account
intro: Sign in starts Tracker and Deskbar as the account whose password worked. A standard account uses /boot/home/users/, with its own Trash and the usual desktop links. The administrator stays on /boot/home. There is still one screen.

title: Keep autologin; run dstcheck as the session user
intro: Login starts dstcheck, UserBootscript (if present), and first-login PostInstallScript after Deskbar. defaultdeskbaritems.sh does not launch ProcessController -deskbar (that was Damned). Tray stays r5-tray / desklink.

title: Move the first administrator off uid 0
intro: After a valid password, Login migrates user off uid 0 (registrar delete + add at a free uid ≥ 1000) and keeps a locked root at uid 0. Tracker and Deskbar start through r5-desktop as that person. Login stays uid 0 so Sign in and Log out still work.

title: Per-user settings audit, Joysticks, find_directory copies
intro: Desktop prefs and most image apps already use finddirectory. MidiPlayer, Joysticks, and PoorMan now live as native copies under distro/user-paths (apply copies files). Joysticks is on the image. Preflet split: personal vs machine (Network, Screen, Time).

title: Make extra home folders private (build 10006)
intro: Other accounts could list /boot/home/Desktop and the rest of the first home. Extra people live under /boot/home/users/, so /boot/home itself must stay traversable.

intro: PR #43 is merged. This is the follow-up from the live image. Installer Quit() relaunches FirstBootPrompt when Deskbar is not running. That is the live cancel-install path.

title: Add Deskbar Log out back to Sign in (build 10005)
intro: Sign in stayed up for the whole session. There was no way back to the card without powering off. Deskbar leaf Log out (confirm) now tears down the desktop target and returns to Sign in.

title: Put a native Sign in screen on the boot path (build 10004)
intro: The live image used to start Tracker and Deskbar on initialvolumesmounted. There was no gate: anyone with the VM reached the desktop. This puts Haiku Login on the boot path (run { login }). FirstBootPrompt Try R5OS starts login, not desktop.
